newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down, stk mkt outflow feared.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down, stk mkt outflow feared.

text.p: * Central Bank also seen buying dollars at 26.359
The Philippine peso ended weak on Tuesday at 26.368 from the previous close of 26.361 on fears of dollar outflows from stock market investments, dealers said.
The stock exchange's key index fell on Tuesday by 2.87 percent to 2,860.45 points on worries on the property sector.
"Some are anticipating outflows from the stock market," a foreign bank dealer said.
The day's average, however, was unchanged at 26.362.
Volume rose to $166.5 million from $131.5 million.
Early in the day, banks were selling dollars as inflows came in from overseas workers' remttances and fixed income investments.
Traders said the Central Bank came in late in the morning to buy about $17 million at 26.359, which prevented the peso from strengthening further through the rest of the session.
As a result of the Central Bank's action and the possibility of outflows from the stock market, the peso could trade in the range of 26.363/26.37 on Wednesday, a dealer said.
